appearance_facts.fact: The line begins near the 1,000–1,100 level at 1880, rises modestly to about 1,100 at 1881, peaks near 1,600 at 1882, dips to about 1,300 at 1883, then climbs gradually to roughly 1,500 at 1884 and 1,650 at 1885.
The line jumps sharply to about 2,400 at 1886, eases slightly to about 2,350 at 1887, and holds near 2,300–2,350 at 1888.
The line rises steeply to about 3,100–3,200 at 1889, reaches its highest point near 3,500–3,600 at 1890, then falls to about 3,200 at 1891.
Despite the title wording, the plotted series shows a net increase from the low-1,000s in 1880 to the low-3,000s by 1891, with a late-period peak at 1890.
Y-axis is labeled 'Number of Tourists' with ticks at 0, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000, 2,500, 3,000, 3,500; X-axis is labeled 'Year' with integer ticks from 1880 through 1891.
The chart title reads 'Decreasing Number of New Tourists in Town Z from 1880 to 1891,' which conflicts with the visible upward trajectory of the plotted line.
